items.name: format
items.summary: Render runtime values with a Go-style formatting template.
details: The first argument is a `string` template. Remaining Osiris values are converted to host-facing scalar or aggregate representations and supplied to the template in source order.

Use ordinary interpolation-free text helpers when a host formatting verb is unnecessary; malformed or mismatched verbs are rendered according to the underlying formatter rather than parsed as Osiris syntax.
items.errors: At least one argument is required, and the first argument must be a `string`.

items.name: compare
items.summary: Perform a locale-independent three-way lexical comparison.
details: The result is `-1i64` when `left` sorts before `right`, `0i64` when they are equal, and `1i64` when `left` sorts after `right`.
Valid UTF-8 text is ordered lexicographically by Unicode code point. Empty strings compare before non-empty strings.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: equal_fold
items.summary: Test strings for equality with Unicode simple case folding.
details: The comparison is locale-independent and follows Unicode simple folding; it does not normalize combining sequences or perform locale-sensitive collation.
Two empty strings compare equal. Greek sigma forms such as `Σ` and `ς` belong to the same simple-fold class.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: contains
items.summary: Report whether a substring occurs in a string.
details: Matching is exact, case-sensitive, and based on complete UTF-8 substring sequences.
The empty needle is present in every string, including the empty string.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: contains_any
items.parameters: `value` is searched for any Unicode code point listed in the `code_points` string.
items.summary: Report whether a string contains any member of a Unicode code-point set.
details: `code_points` is a set of characters, not a substring, byte set, or regular expression.
An empty code-point set always returns `false`, including for an empty input.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: has_prefix
items.summary: Report whether a string begins with an exact prefix.
details: The comparison is case-sensitive and does not normalize Unicode.
Every string has the empty prefix.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: has_suffix
items.summary: Report whether a string ends with an exact suffix.
details: The comparison is case-sensitive and does not normalize Unicode.
Every string has the empty suffix.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: count
items.summary: Count non-overlapping occurrences of a substring.
details: Repeated matches do not overlap, so `count("aaaa", "aa")` is `2u64`.
An empty needle matches before the first code point and after every code point: the result is one plus the Unicode code-point count.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: index
items.summary: Find the first occurrence of a substring by Unicode code-point index.
details: A match returns `some(index)` and an absent needle returns `none()`; there is no `-1` sentinel.
Indexes count Unicode code points rather than UTF-8 bytes. An empty needle returns `some(0u64)`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: index_any
items.parameters: `value` is searched for any Unicode code point listed in the `code_points` string.
items.summary: Find the first member of a Unicode code-point set.
details: The result is a zero-based Unicode code-point index, not a UTF-8 byte offset.
An empty set or an absent member returns `none()`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: last_index
items.summary: Find the last occurrence of a substring by Unicode code-point index.
details: A match returns `some(index)` and an absent needle returns `none()`.
An empty needle matches at the end and returns the Unicode code-point length of `value`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: last_index_any
items.parameters: `value` is searched backward for any Unicode code point listed in the `code_points` string.
items.summary: Find the last member of a Unicode code-point set.
details: The result is a zero-based Unicode code-point index, not a UTF-8 byte offset.
An empty set or an absent member returns `none()`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: cut
items.summary: Cut a string around the first separator.
details: A present separator returns `some([before, after])`, excluding the separator; an absent separator returns `none()`.
The empty separator is present at the start and returns `some(["", value])`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: cut_prefix
items.summary: Remove an exact prefix and report whether it was present.
details: A present prefix returns the remaining string in `some`; an absent prefix returns `none()`.
The empty prefix is always present and returns the original value.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: cut_suffix
items.summary: Remove an exact suffix and report whether it was present.
details: A present suffix returns the preceding string in `some`; an absent suffix returns `none()`.
The empty suffix is always present and returns the original value.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: fields
items.summary: Split text into non-empty fields separated by Unicode whitespace.
details: Runs of spaces, tabs, newlines, and other Unicode whitespace act as one boundary and do not create empty fields.
An empty or whitespace-only input returns an empty list.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: split_after
items.summary: Split after every separator, retaining each separator in its preceding part.
details: Adjacent and trailing separators are preserved in the returned pieces instead of being discarded.
An empty separator splits after each Unicode code point. Empty input with an empty separator returns an empty list.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: split_n
items.parameters: `value` and `separator` are UTF-8 strings. `n` is an exact integral default number, signed/unsigned integer, or `bigint` that fits the host allocation index width.
items.summary: Split around a separator with an explicit result limit.
details: `n < 0` returns every substring, `n == 0` returns an empty list, and positive `n` returns at most `n` substrings with the unsplit remainder in the last element.
An empty separator splits between Unicode code points; a positive limit still bounds the result count.
items.errors: Wrong arity, invalid kinds, a non-integral limit, or a limit outside the host allocation index width produces a structured error.

items.name: split_after_n
items.parameters: `value` and `separator` are UTF-8 strings. `n` is an exact integral default number, signed/unsigned integer, or `bigint` that fits the host allocation index width.
items.summary: Split after a separator with an explicit result limit.
details: `n < 0` returns every part, `n == 0` returns an empty list, and positive `n` returns at most `n` parts with the unsplit remainder in the last element.
Matched separators remain attached to their preceding parts. An empty separator splits after Unicode code points.
items.errors: Wrong arity, invalid kinds, a non-integral limit, or a limit outside the host allocation index width produces a structured error.

items.name: trim_space
items.summary: Remove leading and trailing Unicode whitespace.
details: The whitespace definition includes non-ASCII Unicode space code points.
An empty string and a whitespace-only string both return an empty string. `trim` is the preserved original spelling.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: trim_left
items.parameters: `value` is trimmed from the start while its code points belong to the set listed in `code_points`.
items.summary: Remove a Unicode code-point set from the start of a string.
details: `code_points` is a character set, not a prefix, substring, byte set, or regular expression.
An empty set leaves the value unchanged.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: trim_right
items.parameters: `value` is trimmed from the end while its code points belong to the set listed in `code_points`.
items.summary: Remove a Unicode code-point set from the end of a string.
details: `code_points` is a character set, not a suffix, substring, byte set, or regular expression.
An empty set leaves the value unchanged.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: trim_prefix
items.summary: Remove one exact prefix when present.
details: Unlike `cut_prefix`, absence is not represented separately: an absent prefix returns the original value.
An empty prefix also leaves the value unchanged.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: trim_suffix
items.summary: Remove one exact suffix when present.
details: Unlike `cut_suffix`, absence is not represented separately: an absent suffix returns the original value.
An empty suffix also leaves the value unchanged.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string argument produces a structured `invalid_argument` or `type_error`.

items.name: replace_n
items.parameters: `value`, `old`, and `replacement` are UTF-8 strings. `n` is an exact integral default number, signed/unsigned integer, or `bigint` that fits the host allocation index width.
items.summary: Replace a bounded number of non-overlapping substring occurrences.
details: `n < 0` replaces every occurrence, `n == 0` returns the original value, and positive `n` replaces at most the first `n` matches.
An empty `old` value matches before the first code point and after each code point; `n` still limits inserted replacements.
items.errors: Wrong arity, invalid kinds, a non-integral or out-of-range limit, or a result too large for the host allocation limit produces a structured error.

items.name: pi
items.summary: Read the standard-library circle constants.
details: `math.pi` is π and `math.tau` is 2π. They are immutable `number` values exported by `std/math`.
Global named constants `Pi`/`pi` and `Tau`/`tau` are also available; the qualified spellings make the module dependency explicit.

items.name: atan2
items.parameters: `y` and `x` are `number`, `f32`, `f64`, or bfloat values. Exact integers and decimal families require an explicit floating conversion.
items.summary: Return the quadrant-aware angle of the point `(x, y)` in radians.
details: The result lies in `[-Pi, Pi]` and retains the promoted floating width and style of both arguments.
IEEE signed zeros, infinities, and NaNs determine the quadrant and exceptional result without host error text.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: exp2
items.summary: Compute two raised to a floating-point power.
details: The result retains the input floating width and style. Finite underflow produces positive zero.
NaN and infinite inputs follow IEEE behavior; a finite input whose result overflows its retained width is rejected.
items.errors: Finite overflow produces structured `out_of_range`; wrong arity or kind also produces a structured error.

items.name: trunc
items.summary: Round a floating value toward zero without changing its family.
details: Fractional digits are discarded and the input width and bfloat style are retained.
Signed zero, NaN, and infinity are preserved according to IEEE arithmetic.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: fmod
items.parameters: Both arguments are floating-point numbers; `divisor` must be non-zero.
items.summary: Return the truncating floating-point remainder.
details: The result is `dividend - trunc(dividend / divisor) * divisor`, carries the dividend's sign, and uses the promoted floating style.
NaN and infinity otherwise follow IEEE remainder behavior.
items.errors: A zero divisor produces structured `invalid_argument`; wrong arity or kind also produces a structured error.

items.name: remainder
items.parameters: Both arguments are floating-point numbers; `divisor` must be non-zero.
items.summary: Return the IEEE remainder using a nearest-integer quotient.
details: The quotient is rounded to the nearest integer with ties to even before the product is subtracted.
The result uses the promoted floating width and can differ in sign from `fmod`.
items.errors: A zero divisor produces structured `invalid_argument`; wrong arity or kind also produces a structured error.

items.name: fma
items.parameters: All three arguments are floating-point numbers.
items.summary: Compute `x * y + addend` with one fused rounding step.
details: The host fused operation is evaluated once and then narrowed to the promoted Osiris floating family.
Overflow, NaN, infinity, and signed-zero results remain IEEE floating values.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: positive_difference
items.summary: Return `x - y` when positive, otherwise positive zero.
details: The result uses the promoted floating family and always returns `+0` for a finite non-positive difference.
If subtraction is indeterminate, including equal infinities, the result is NaN.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: copysign
items.summary: Copy only the sign bit of one floating value onto another.
details: The absolute value comes from `magnitude`; the sign bit, including negative zero or a signed NaN, comes from `sign`.
The result uses the promoted floating width and style.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: nextafter
items.summary: Step from one floating value to its adjacent representable value toward another.
details: Fully `f32` arguments use the adjacent `f32` value; default and `f64` forms use the adjacent binary64 value.
Equal inputs return `toward`, preserving its signed zero. NaNs propagate.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: frexp
items.summary: Decompose a floating value into a binary fraction and exponent.
details: The two-element result is `[fraction, exponent]` with `value == fraction * 2^exponent`; non-zero finite fractions have magnitude in `[0.5, 1)`.
The fraction retains the input floating family. Zero, infinity, and NaN return exponent `0i64`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: ldexp
items.parameters: `fraction` is floating-point; `exponent` is an exact default, signed, unsigned, or `bigint` integer in host range.
items.summary: Scale a floating value by an exact power of two.
details: The result is `fraction * 2^exponent` rounded once to the fraction's retained floating family.
Finite underflow returns a signed zero. NaN and infinity propagate.
items.errors: An out-of-range exponent or finite overflow produces structured `out_of_range`; invalid kinds and arity are also structured.

items.name: modf
items.summary: Split a floating value into integral and fractional parts.
details: The two-element result is `[integer, fraction]`; both elements retain the input floating family.
Both parts preserve the input sign for zero. Infinity yields `[infinity, signed zero]`; NaN yields two NaNs.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: isfinite
items.summary: Report whether every component is finite.
details: A real value is finite when it is neither infinity nor NaN.
A complex value is finite only when both real and imaginary components are finite.
items.errors: Wrong arity or another value kind produces a structured error.

items.name: isinf
items.summary: Report whether a value contains an infinity.
details: A real value is infinite when it is positive or negative infinity.
A complex value is infinite when either component is infinite, even if the other component is NaN.
items.errors: Wrong arity or another value kind produces a structured error.

items.name: isnan
items.summary: Report whether a value is NaN.
details: A real value is NaN when its IEEE payload represents not-a-number.
A complex value is NaN when either component is NaN and neither component is infinite.
items.errors: Wrong arity or another value kind produces a structured error.

items.name: isnormal
items.summary: Report whether a floating value is finite, non-zero, and not subnormal.
details: The normal threshold follows binary32 for explicit widths through `32` and binary64 for default or wider families.
Zero, subnormal values, infinities, and NaNs return `false`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: signbit
items.summary: Inspect the sign bit of a floating value.
details: Negative finite values, negative infinity, and negative zero return `true`.
The sign bit is inspected directly; the operation does not compare the value with zero.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: degrees
items.summary: Convert an angle from radians to degrees.
details: The conversion multiplies by `180 / Pi` and retains the input floating family.
Infinity and NaN follow ordinary IEEE multiplication.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: radians
items.summary: Convert an angle from degrees to radians.
details: The conversion multiplies by `Pi / 180` and retains the input floating family.
Infinity and NaN follow ordinary IEEE multiplication.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: sinpi
items.parameters: `x` is a floating-point number measured in half-turns.
items.summary: Compute `sin(Pi * x)` with exact integer and half-integer reduction.
details: Integer inputs return exact signed zero and half-integers return exact `-1` or `1`, avoiding multiplication-rounding noise.
Finite values are reduced modulo two before evaluation; infinity and NaN produce NaN.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: cospi
items.parameters: `x` is a floating-point number measured in half-turns.
items.summary: Compute `cos(Pi * x)` with exact integer and half-integer reduction.
details: Integer inputs return exact `-1` or `1`; half-integers return exact positive zero.
Finite values are reduced modulo two before evaluation; infinity and NaN produce NaN.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-floating argument produces a structured error.

items.name: tanpi
items.parameters: `x` is a floating-point number measured in half-turns.
items.summary: Compute `tan(Pi * x)` with exact period reduction.
details: Integer inputs return exact signed zero and quarter-turns return exact `-1` or `1`.
Half-integers are mathematical poles and are rejected instead of returning a platform-dependent large finite value.
items.errors: A half-integer produces structured `invalid_argument`; wrong arity or kind also produces a structured error.

items.name: divmod
items.parameters: Arguments are exact `int`, `uint`, `bigint`, or integral default-number values; `divisor` must be non-zero.
items.summary: Compute an exact integer quotient and remainder together.
details: The two-element result is `[quotient, remainder]`, with quotient truncated toward zero and remainder carrying the dividend's sign.
Matching signed or unsigned fixed-width inputs retain their family; mixed or arbitrary-precision inputs return exact `bigint` elements.
items.errors: A zero divisor produces structured `invalid_argument`; non-integral values, unsupported exact families, and wrong arity are structured errors.

items.name: gcd
items.parameters: `a` and `b` are exact `int`, `uint`, `bigint`, or integral default-number values.
items.summary: Compute the greatest common divisor of two exact integers.
details: The result is always non-negative and `gcd(0, 0)` is zero.
Two unsigned fixed-width inputs retain their promoted width and packed style; other input combinations return `bigint`.
items.errors: Non-integral values, unsupported exact families, or wrong arity produce a structured error.

items.name: lcm
items.parameters: `a` and `b` are exact `int`, `uint`, `bigint`, or integral default-number values.
items.summary: Compute the least common multiple of two exact integers.
details: The result is zero when either input is zero and is otherwise `abs(a / gcd(a, b) * b)`.
Two unsigned inputs retain their promoted width when the result fits; overflow widens to `bigint` rather than wrapping.
items.errors: Non-integral values, unsupported exact families, or wrong arity produce a structured error.

items.name: count_ones
items.parameters: `value` is an explicit fixed-width unsigned value, including packed `ufN` families.
items.summary: Count set bits across the value's declared width.
details: The count includes every one bit from bit zero through `width - 1`.
Zero returns `0u64`; the input value and packed style are not changed.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-unsigned value produces a structured error.

items.name: count_zeros
items.parameters: `value` is an explicit fixed-width unsigned value, including packed `ufN` families.
items.summary: Count zero bits across the value's declared width.
details: The result is the declared width minus `count_ones(value)`.
Zero therefore returns the full declared width.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-unsigned value produces a structured error.

items.name: leading_zeros
items.parameters: `value` is an explicit fixed-width unsigned value, including packed `ufN` families.
items.summary: Count zero bits before the highest set bit.
details: The declared width, rather than a host machine word, defines the left edge.
Zero returns the full declared width.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-unsigned value produces a structured error.

items.name: trailing_zeros
items.parameters: `value` is an explicit fixed-width unsigned value, including packed `ufN` families.
items.summary: Count zero bits after the lowest set bit.
details: Counting begins at bit zero and stops at the first one bit.
Zero returns the full declared width.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-unsigned value produces a structured error.

items.name: bit_width
items.parameters: `value` is an explicit fixed-width unsigned value, including packed `ufN` families.
items.summary: Return the number of bits needed to represent an unsigned value.
details: A non-zero result is one more than the index of the highest set bit.
Zero has bit width `0u64`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-unsigned value produces a structured error.

items.name: bit_floor
items.parameters: `value` is an explicit fixed-width unsigned value, including packed `ufN` families.
items.summary: Return the greatest power of two no larger than an unsigned value.
details: Zero returns zero. Every non-zero result contains exactly one set bit.
The declared width and packed/native style are retained.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-unsigned value produces a structured error.

items.name: bit_ceil
items.parameters: `value` is an explicit fixed-width unsigned value, including packed `ufN` families.
items.summary: Return the least power of two no smaller than an unsigned value.
details: Zero and one return one. Existing powers of two are unchanged.
The declared width and packed/native style are retained; a next power outside that width never wraps.
items.errors: An unrepresentable next power produces structured `out_of_range`; wrong arity or kind also produces a structured error.

items.name: has_single_bit
items.parameters: `value` is an explicit fixed-width unsigned value, including packed `ufN` families.
items.summary: Report whether an unsigned value is a non-zero power of two.
details: Exactly one bit must be set inside the declared width.
Zero returns `false`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-unsigned value produces a structured error.

items.name: byte_swap
items.parameters: `value` is a byte-aligned fixed-width unsigned value, including packed `ufN` families.
items.summary: Reverse byte order across an unsigned value's full declared width.
details: Bits inside each byte keep their order; only the byte positions are reversed.
The result preserves width and packed/native style, including widths greater than 64 bits.
items.errors: Non-byte-aligned widths produce structured `unsupported`; wrong arity or kind also produces a structured error.

items.name: phase
items.summary: Return a complex value's phase angle in radians.
details: The result lies in `[-Pi, Pi]` and retains the complex component width.
Signed imaginary zero selects the side of the negative-real branch cut: `-1+0i` has phase `Pi`, while `-1-0i` has phase `-Pi`.
items.errors: Wrong arity or a non-complex value produces a structured error.

items.name: clone
items.summary: Create a tensor with independent shape and element storage.
details: `clone` preserves the source tensor's shape and values while allocating independent backing slices.
Use it at an ownership boundary when subsequent implementation-level mutation must not alias the original tensor.
items.errors: Exactly one `tensor` argument is required.

items.name: view
items.summary: Create a tensor value that shares shape and element storage.
details: `view` is the explicit aliasing counterpart to `clone`: it returns the same logical shape and values but shares backing slices.
Osiris source operations are value-oriented today; the alias remains relevant to optimizer, host-integration, and future mutable-buffer ownership analysis.
items.errors: Exactly one `tensor` argument is required.

items.name: read_async
items.syntax:
read_async(path)
readbytes_async(path)
write_async(path, data)
lines_async(data)
csv_async(data)
jsonparse_async(data)
items.summary: Run one blocking file or data helper inside an explicit task.
details: Arguments are evaluated before the task is created. The matching blocking operation then runs inside the task and its value or structured failure is observed with `await`.
These wrappers do not change the underlying file format or parsing contract. They provide task composition; they do not expose an operating-system asynchronous file API.
items.errors: Arity, type, file, encoding, and parse failures are retained by the task and propagate from `await`. An active session is required.
items.example:
let pending = read_async("__OSIRIS_DOC_TMP__/input.txt")
emit await(pending) # "first line\nsecond line\n"

items.name: json
items.summary: Serialize one Osiris value to JSON text.
details: `json` uses the public value codec for scalars and supported aggregate values, including structured enum and error records.
Use `jsonparse` for the inverse text-to-value direction. Some runtime resources such as tasks, streams, functions, and modules are not serializable values.
items.errors: Exactly one serializable value is required; unsupported runtime resources produce an error.

items.name: band
items.syntax:
band(a, b, values...)
bor(a, b, values...)
bxor(a, b, values...)
items.summary: Fold bitwise AND, OR, or XOR across two or more unsigned values.
details: The result preserves the selected unsigned width and packed style. Every operation is masked to that width.
The infix spellings `&`, `|`, and `^` perform the corresponding binary operation.
items.errors: At least two unsigned integer-compatible arguments are required.
items.example:
emit band(0xf0u8, 0x3cu8)
emit bor(0x10u8, 0x03u8)
emit bxor(0xffu8, 0x0fu8)

items.name: bnot
items.summary: Invert every bit inside an unsigned value's declared width.
details: `bnot` preserves width and packed style and is equivalent to the unary `~` operator.
Bits outside the declared width are discarded.
items.errors: Exactly one unsigned integer-compatible value is required.

items.name: shl
items.summary: Shift an unsigned value left or right within its declared width.
details: `shl` and `shr` are function spellings for `<<` and `>>`. Results retain the left operand's width and packed style.
For the ordinary width-at-most-64 path, the shift count is reduced modulo 64; values are masked after a left shift.
items.errors: Exactly two unsigned integer-compatible arguments are required; an unrepresentable wide shift count is rejected.

items.name: rotl
items.summary: Rotate an unsigned value left or right inside its declared bit width.
details: Rotation wraps displaced bits around the other edge and preserves the input width and packed style.
The count is reduced modulo the declared width, so rotating by a full width returns the same value.
items.errors: Exactly two unsigned integer-compatible arguments are required; an unrepresentable wide count is rejected.

items.name: fixed-width bit inspection
items.parameters: `value` is an explicit fixed-width unsigned or packed unsigned value.
items.returns: a `u64` count, `bool`, or width-preserving unsigned result, depending on the selected operation
items.summary: Inspect bit populations and boundaries or transform byte order without losing declared width.
details: The complete family is `count_ones`, `count_zeros`, `leading_zeros`, `trailing_zeros`, `bit_width`, `bit_floor`, `bit_ceil`, `has_single_bit`, and `byte_swap`.
Their individual `std/math` listings define zero, overflow, packed-style, and byte-alignment behavior. These helpers never substitute the host machine word width.
items.errors: Invalid kinds, wrong arity, an unrepresentable `bit_ceil`, or a non-byte-aligned `byte_swap` produce structured errors.

groups.title: Constants and Units
groups.summary: Global mathematical constants, physical constants, metric prefixes, units, and structured-error kind values.

items.name: SI base units
items.syntax:
Meter | meter | m
Second | second | s
Kilogram | kilogram | kg
Ampere | ampere | A
Kelvin | kelvin | K
Mole | mole | mol
Candela | candela | cd
items.summary: Use the seven SI base-unit values in long, lowercase, or symbol form.
details: Each spelling denotes a unit-magnitude `quantity` with a canonical dimension. Aliases are equal values; choose the spelling that is clearest in the surrounding expression.
Multiply or divide numeric values and units explicitly, for example `3 * meter` or `10 * m / s`.

items.name: SI derived units
items.syntax: Hertz | Hz; Newton | N; Pascal | Pa; Joule | J; Watt | W; Coulomb | C; Volt | V; Farad | F; Ohm; Siemens | S; Weber | Wb; Tesla | T; Henry | H; Lumen | lm; Lux | lx; Becquerel | Bq; Gray | Gy; Sievert | Sv; Katal | kat
items.summary: Use named SI derived-unit values with their canonical dimension vectors.
details: Long names also have lowercase aliases. Symbols are case-sensitive: `Pa`, `Wb`, `Gy`, and `Sv` are distinct identifiers.
Derived units participate in the same exact quantity arithmetic and compatibility checks as products of base units.

items.name: time and volume units
items.syntax:
Liter | liter | litre | L
Minute | minute | min
Hour | hour | h
Day | day | d
Week | week
items.summary: Use common scaled volume and time quantities.
details: `Liter` is exactly one thousandth of a cubic `Meter`; the time units are exact multiples of `Second`.
These names are ordinary immutable global values, not numeric suffixes.

items.name: mathematical constants
items.syntax: Pi | pi; Tau | tau; E | e; Phi | phi; Percent | percent
items.summary: Use built-in circle, exponential, golden-ratio, and percentage constants.
details: `Pi`, `Tau`, `E`, and `Phi` use the runtime's default floating `number` representation. `Percent` is `0.01`.
Uppercase and lowercase spellings are equal immutable values. `std/math` also exports qualified `pi` and `tau`.

items.name: physical constants
items.syntax:
SpeedOfLight | speedOfLight | c0
Planck | planck; ReducedPlanck | reducedPlanck | hbar
Avogadro | avogadro | NA; Boltzmann | boltzmann | kB
GasConstant | gasConstant | R; ElementaryCharge | elementaryCharge | q_e
GravitationalConstant | gravitationalConstant | G
StandardGravity | standardGravity | g0; FineStructure | fineStructure | alpha
items.summary: Use checked-in mathematical representations of common physical constants.
details: Constants with dimensions are exact decimal `quantity` values; dimensionless constants are `number` values. Names and aliases are case-sensitive identifiers.
These values are deterministic language constants, not a metrology database. Code requiring a particular standards edition should record that requirement alongside its inputs.

items.name: metric prefixes
items.syntax:
kilo mega giga tera peta exa
milli micro nano pico centi deci deca hecto
items.summary: Scale values with immutable decimal metric-prefix factors.
details: The factors range from `pico` (`10^-12`) through `exa` (`10^18`) and combine with quantities through ordinary multiplication.
A prefix is an ordinary value: write `3 * kilo * meter`; juxtaposed unit literals are not a separate grammar.
items.example:
emit 3 * kilo * meter
emit 250 * micro * second

items.name: error kind constants
items.syntax: UnknownError | InvalidArgument | NotFound | AlreadyExists | PermissionDenied | Unauthenticated | Unavailable | Timeout | Cancelled | Conflict | ResourceExhausted | OutOfMemory | OutOfRange | Unsupported | NotImplemented | ParseError | TypeError | EncodingError | IOError | NetworkError | DatabaseError | InternalError
items.summary: Construct and classify structured errors without spelling unstable message text.
details: Each constant evaluates to its canonical lowercase kind code, for example `InvalidArgument` becomes `"invalid_argument"`.
Pass these values to `error`, `wrap`, `matches`, or `is`; compare kinds rather than parsing user-facing messages.

types.name: stream
types.summary: An owned host-backed readable, writable, or duplex stream handle.

types.name: task
types.summary: A handle to one explicit concurrent evaluation.

types.name: function
types.summary: A callable value with positional parameters and optional lexical captures.

types.name: module
types.summary: A named, versioned namespace of exported values.

types.name: enum
types.summary: A nominal closed case value with optional payload fields.

types.name: tcp_listener
types.summary: An owned host TCP listening resource.

types.name: duration
types.summary: An immutable, exact signed 64-bit nanosecond interval used for elapsed-time arithmetic.

types.name: datetime
types.summary: An immutable nanosecond-precision instant with retained UTC, fixed-offset, or IANA location identity.

types.name: location
types.summary: An immutable UTC, fixed-offset, or IANA timezone rule set used to interpret and display datetimes.

entries.name: comments and statement separators
entries.description: Separate statements with whitespace or semicolons and attach line comments with either supported marker.
entries.parameters: Unicode whitespace is ignored. `#` and `//` consume through the end of the current line. `;` may separate statements explicitly and repeated semicolons are ignored.
entries.returnValue: Comments are discarded by the lexer; separators only delimit syntax.
details: A newline is whitespace rather than a token, so the parser uses complete statement and expression shapes to determine boundaries.
There are no block comments.
entries.example:
let left = 2; let right = 3 // second binding
# the next statement emits the sum
emit left + right
# 5u64

entries.name: identifiers and keywords
entries.description: Name bindings with Unicode-aware identifiers while reserving the language's declaration, control-flow, and literal words.
entries.parameters: Reserved words are `let`, `emit`, `macro`, `func`, `return`, `try`, `catch`, `while`, `for`, `in`, `break`, `continue`, `package`, `export`, `enum`, `import`, `match`, `switch`, `as`, `true`, `false`, and `null`.
entries.returns: An identifier token or a reserved keyword token.
entries.returnValue: Pattern words `default`, `when`, `and`, and `not` are contextual identifiers rather than globally reserved keywords.
details: Identifiers may start with `_` or any Unicode letter. Following characters may also be Unicode digits.
Names are case-sensitive.

entries.name: literal and aggregate expressions
entries.signature: number | "string" | true | false | null | [expressions…] | { statements…; tail }
entries.description: Construct scalar literals, ordered lists, and lexical block expressions directly in source.
entries.parameters: Strings recognize `\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\\`, and `\"`; an unknown escape contributes the escaped character. Lists evaluate items in source order. A block contains statements and an optional final expression.
entries.returns: The literal value, a `list`, or the block's tail value.
entries.returnValue: A block without a tail expression evaluates to `null`; its bindings remain local to that block.
details: List values may contain mixed runtime kinds.
Numeric literal bases, separators, families, and suffixes are specified on the Types page and in the technical reference.

entries.name: operators and evaluation order
entries.description: Apply arithmetic, comparison, bitwise, shift, and logical operations with deterministic left-to-right operand evaluation.
entries.parameters: Binary operators are left-associative. From weakest to strongest: `||`; `&&`; `|`; `^`; `&`; `<<`/`>>`; prefix `-`/`!`/`~` in the current parser; `==`/`!=`; `<`/`<=`/`>`/`>=`; `+`/`-`; `*`/`/`/`%`; then calls, members, and postfix `?`.
entries.returns: An operator-specific scalar, aggregate, or `bool` value.
entries.returnValue: `&&` and `||` short-circuit and return `bool`. Numeric operators preserve width/style according to the operand rules.
details: The current parser's prefix tier is intentionally reported exactly: `-1 + 2` parses as `-(1 + 2)` and evaluates to `-3`. Parenthesize unary operands when combining them with equality, comparison, additive, or multiplicative operators.
The named special forms `and(left, right)` and `or(left, right)` have the same lazy boolean behavior as `&&` and `||`.
entries.example:
emit 2 + 3 * 4
emit false && panic("not evaluated")
emit 0xf0u8 & 0x3cu8

entries.name: calls, members, and propagation
entries.description: Call functions and special forms, resolve module or record members, and propagate fallible values.
entries.parameters: Ordinary call arguments evaluate in source order. Member access resolves modules, enums, and supported structured values. Postfix `?` accepts a `Result` or `Option`.
entries.returns: The callee result, selected member, or unwrapped success/present payload.
entries.returnValue: A failed `Result` or empty `Option` exits the current function boundary with its structured failure.
details: Calls, members, and postfix propagation form the strongest postfix expression tier and may be chained.
`let? name = expression` is the statement-level unwrapping form.
entries.example:
func add1(value) => value + 1
let? value = some(4)
emit add1(value)
# 5u64

entries.name: truthiness
entries.description: Convert any runtime value to the boolean condition used by control-flow and logical forms.
entries.parameters: Falsey values are `null`, `false`, numeric zero, empty text/list/tensor, structured errors, failed `Result` values, and `ok` whose payload is falsey. An empty `Option` is falsey; every present `Option` is truthy even when its payload is falsey.
entries.returns: `bool` when observed through `!`, `&&`, `||`, `and`, or `or`; branch forms use the conversion without returning it.
entries.returnValue: Functions and modules are always truthy. Live streams, tasks, and TCP listeners are truthy.
details: Zero tests preserve each numeric family's representation, including decimal, fixed, interval, modular, complex, dual, bigint, bigfloat, signed, unsigned, and quantity values.
An interval is falsey only when both endpoints are zero.

entries.name: and
entries.description: Evaluate lazy boolean conjunction or disjunction in call-shaped syntax.
entries.parameters: Both forms accept exactly two expressions. `and` skips `right` when `left` is falsey; `or` skips it when `left` is truthy.
entries.returnValue: The result is the truthiness of the selected evaluation path, not either original operand.
details: `and` and `or` are evaluator special forms, so the skipped expression is never evaluated.
They correspond to infix `&&` and `||`.
entries.errors: Wrong arity is an error; an error from an expression that is actually evaluated propagates.
entries.example:
emit and(false, panic("skipped"))
emit or(true, panic("skipped"))

entries.name: ok
entries.description: Construct successful and failed `Result` values.
entries.parameters: `ok` takes one payload. `err` takes one structured error or one `string` message; a message creates an `unknown_error` record.
entries.returnValue: `ok(value)` retains the payload; `err(value)` retains or constructs the structured failure.
details: Result records are immutable and preserve must-handle metadata through supported combinators.
Use `error(kind, message)` when the failure requires a stable non-unknown kind.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or an `err` argument that is neither an error nor string-compatible is an error.

entries.name: some
entries.description: Construct present and absent `Option` values.
entries.parameters: `some` accepts exactly one payload. `none` accepts no arguments.
entries.returnValue: `some(value)` is present even when `value` is falsey; `none()` is absent.
details: Option records are immutable.
Unwrapping `none()` produces a structured `not_found` failure.
entries.errors: Wrong arity is an error.

entries.name: isok
entries.description: Inspect fallibility containers without unwrapping them.
entries.parameters: Each predicate accepts exactly one value. `iserr` also returns `true` for a bare structured error.
entries.returnValue: A value of the wrong container family produces `false`, not a type error.
details: `isnone` returns `true` only for an empty `Option`; ordinary non-option values return `false`.
Payload truthiness does not affect these structural predicates.
entries.errors: Only wrong arity is an error.

entries.name: unwrap
entries.description: Extract a fallible payload, replace failure with context, or supply a plain fallback value.
entries.parameters: `unwrap` takes one `Result`, `Option`, or error. `expect` and `or_else` take a container plus a message or fallback.
entries.returns: The contained payload, selected fallback, or an error value when unwrapping an error cause.
entries.returnValue: `unwrap` propagates a failed `Result` or absent `Option`; `expect` replaces that failure with the supplied message; `or_else` returns its fallback without evaluating a callback.
details: For a structured error, `unwrap` returns its cause when present and otherwise returns the error itself as a value.
`expect` uses `invalid_argument` for a failed `Result` and `not_found` for an empty `Option`.
entries.errors: Wrong arity and unsupported input kinds are errors.

entries.name: map
entries.signature:
map(result, function)
map_error(result, function)
flat_map(result, function)
entries.description: Transform successful payloads, failed errors, or chain fallible computations lazily.
entries.parameters: Each form takes one `Result` expression and one function. `map` calls it only for success; `map_error` only for failure; `flat_map` only for success.
entries.returnValue: `map` wraps the callback value in `ok`; `map_error` expects an error or message; `flat_map` expects a `Result` or `Option`.
details: A skipped callback is not invoked. Existing failures and must-handle metadata are preserved.
An empty `Option` returned by `flat_map` becomes `err(not_found)`.
entries.errors: Wrong arity, a non-`Result` input, a non-callable callback, or a callback result of the wrong family is an error.
entries.example:
func double(value) => value * 2
func next(value) => some(value + 1)
emit map(ok(3), double)
emit flat_map(ok(4), next)

entries.name: error
entries.signature:
error(kind, message)
wrap(cause, kind, message)
cause(error)
entries.description: Construct a structured error, add a causal wrapper, or inspect the immediate cause.
entries.parameters: `kind` and `message` are string-compatible values. `wrap` accepts an error or `null` cause. `cause` accepts one error.
entries.returnValue: Construction preserves stable kind/code and message fields; `cause` returns `null` when no cause is attached.
details: Errors are immutable. Wrapping constructs a new record and leaves the cause unchanged.
Use named error-kind constants instead of parsing or depending on display text.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or values that cannot satisfy the error/string contracts are errors.

entries.name: withmeta
entries.signature:
withmeta(error, key, value)
withdebug(error, key, value)
errmeta(error)
redact(error)
entries.description: Attach immutable public or debug metadata, inspect public fields, and remove sensitive error details.
entries.parameters: Mutation-like helpers take an error, string key, and value. `errmeta` and `redact` each take one error.
entries.returns: A copied `error`, or a public key/value `list` from `errmeta`.
entries.returnValue: `redact` strips stack and debug-only metadata recursively while preserving the public cause chain.
details: Recognized public keys update canonical fields; other public keys remain in the generic metadata map.
Debug metadata is excluded from `errmeta` and ordinary serialization.
entries.errors: Wrong arity, non-error inputs, and non-string metadata keys are errors.

entries.name: matches
entries.description: Compare a structured error's stable kind or code without inspecting message text.
entries.parameters: One structured error and one string-compatible kind/code value.
entries.returnValue: Comparison is case-insensitive against both the record kind and code.
details: `is` is an exact alias for `matches`.
Named error-kind constants provide the canonical values.
entries.errors: Wrong arity, a non-error first argument, or a non-string-compatible kind is an error.

entries.name: panic
entries.description: Raise a fatal structured internal error or assert an invariant.
entries.parameters: `panic` and `trap` take one string-compatible message. `assert` takes a condition and message.
entries.returns: `assert` returns `true` when its condition is truthy; the failing paths do not return normally.
entries.returnValue: A failure has `internal_error` kind and fatal severity and bypasses ordinary `catch` recovery.
details: `trap` is an alias for `panic`.
Use these for impossible states, not expected recoverable failures.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a non-string-compatible message is an error; a falsey assertion deliberately raises a fatal error.

entries.name: spawn
entries.description: Start evaluating one expression in an explicit task.
entries.parameters: Exactly one unevaluated expression and an active runtime session.
entries.returnValue: The task handle is returned immediately; its value, output, error, or cancellation is observed by `await`.
details: The expression runs with the current lexical scope and cooperative session context.
Use `parallel` for a fixed group whose results and output must be committed in argument order.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or use without an active session is an error.

entries.name: await
entries.description: Wait for a task and merge its ordered output into the current session.
entries.parameters: Exactly one expression that evaluates to a `task`.
entries.returnValue: Task errors and cancellation propagate as structured failures.
details: `await` is a suspension and error-propagation boundary.
Awaiting does not erase value kind, numeric width, tensor shape, or error metadata.
entries.errors: Wrong arity, a non-task value, or the task's own failure is an error.

entries.name: cancel
entries.description: Request cooperative cancellation of one task.
entries.parameters: Exactly one expression that evaluates to a `task`.
entries.returnValue: `true` only when this call newly requested cancellation; repeated or already-complete cancellation returns `false`.
details: Cancellation is observed at runtime safe points and task-aware waits.
A blocking host operation is cancellable only when its documented implementation observes the session context.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a non-task value is an error.

entries.name: parallel
entries.description: Evaluate a fixed set of branches concurrently and preserve source-visible ordering.
entries.parameters: Zero or more unevaluated expressions and an active session.
entries.returnValue: Result positions and branch `emit` output are committed in argument order, regardless of completion order.
details: A branch failure cancels sibling work and propagates.
`parallel()` returns an empty list.
entries.errors: A branch error or use without an active session is an error.

entries.name: timeout
entries.description: Evaluate one expression under a cooperative deadline.
entries.parameters: A non-negative integer millisecond duration and one unevaluated expression.
entries.returnValue: Output is committed only after successful completion before the deadline.
details: The body runs in a child session with a deadline-bearing context.
Timeout cannot forcibly interrupt host work that does not observe cancellation.
entries.errors: Wrong arity, an invalid duration, body failure, or deadline expiry is an error.

entries.name: race
entries.description: Return the first completed branch, optionally with its source index.
entries.parameters: One or more unevaluated expressions and an active session.
entries.returns: The winning value from `race`; `[index, value]` from `select`.
entries.returnValue: Only the winning branch's buffered output is committed. The remaining branches receive cooperative cancellation.
details: In ordinary execution, completion order chooses the winner. In deterministic task-debug mode, the first source branch wins.
`select` reports a zero-based `u64` source index.
entries.errors: No arguments, use without a session, or a winning branch failure is an error.

entries.name: number
entries.description: Explicitly convert one numeric-compatible value to the default floating `number` family.
entries.parameters: Exactly one value accepted by floating conversion.
entries.returnValue: The conversion uses the `f64` numeric conversion path and clears the explicit-width marker.
details: This is an explicit conversion. A typed `let` annotation is a constraint and does not perform the same cast.
Precision loss is possible when converting exact or wide values to the default floating family.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a value without a numeric conversion is an error.
entries.example:
let value number = 4
emit value
emit number(4)
# 4
# 4

entries.name: dec
entries.description: Convert one numeric or textual value to the exact decimal family.
entries.parameters: Exactly one `decimal`, numeric-compatible value, or decimal `string`.
entries.returnValue: `dec` is the global short spelling used by `decimal`, `rat`, and `rational` conversion paths.
details: String input is parsed as exact decimal text; existing decimal input is copied.
Use the longer constructor names when they communicate intent better.
entries.errors: Wrong arity, malformed decimal text, or an unsupported input kind is an error.

entries.name: map
entries.description: An ordered collection of key/value entries.
entries.parameters: Keys and values may use the existing runtime value families.
entries.returnValue: Map iteration yields keys in insertion order.
details: Use map_new, map_set, map_get, map_keys, and map_values for explicit construction and access.

entries.name: set
entries.description: An ordered collection of unique values.
entries.parameters: Values use the existing equality contract.
entries.returnValue: Set iteration yields unique values in insertion order.
details: Use set_new, set_add, set_has, and set_values for explicit construction and access.

entries.name: map_new
entries.description: Construct an empty ordered map.
entries.parameters: No arguments.
entries.returnValue: A new empty map with deterministic insertion order.
details: Map entries retain deterministic insertion order.
entries.errors: Wrong arity is an error.

entries.name: map_set
entries.description: Set one ordered map entry.
entries.parameters: A map, key, and value.
entries.returnValue: Existing keys retain their position; new keys append in insertion order.
details: Updating a key does not move it.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a non-map first argument is an error.

entries.name: map_get
entries.description: Look up one ordered map entry.
entries.parameters: A map and key.
entries.returnValue: Missing keys return `null`.
details: Lookup does not mutate the map.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a non-map first argument is an error.

entries.name: map_keys
entries.description: Return ordered map keys.
entries.parameters: One map.
entries.returnValue: Keys follow insertion order.
details: The returned list is a snapshot of the key order.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a non-map argument is an error.

entries.name: map_values
entries.description: Return ordered map values.
entries.parameters: One map.
entries.returnValue: Values follow their corresponding key order.
details: The returned list is a snapshot of the value order.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a non-map argument is an error.

entries.name: set_new
entries.description: Construct an empty ordered set.
entries.parameters: No arguments.
entries.returnValue: A new empty set with deterministic insertion order.
details: Set membership uses the value equality contract.
entries.errors: Wrong arity is an error.

entries.name: set_add
entries.description: Add one value to an ordered set.
entries.parameters: A set and value.
entries.returnValue: Duplicate values do not create another entry.
details: New values append in insertion order.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a non-set first argument is an error.

entries.name: set_has
entries.description: Test set membership.
entries.parameters: A set and value.
entries.returnValue: Returns true when the value is present.
details: Membership does not change set order.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a non-set first argument is an error.

entries.name: set_values
entries.description: Return ordered set values.
entries.parameters: One set.
entries.returnValue: Values follow insertion order.
details: The returned list is a snapshot of the set order.
entries.errors: Wrong arity or a non-set argument is an error.
